fact_label: Remote work for a foreign employer/clients has no legal visa or work-permit category
value_raw: No official authorization exists — "No visa or permit category covers ordinary remote work for overseas clients"
notes: New fact, 2026-07-18 (Linh, thinnest-3-criteria wave) — Income viability carried zero fact rows before, a genuine gap now closed with the single most load-bearing finding in it. Vietnam's Labor Code (Law 45/2019/QH14), Article 151, requires foreign nationals "working in Vietnam" to hold a valid work permit unless an Article 154 exemption applies; the source states plainly no e-visa work category exists and "officers can ask about your activity." Divergence flag set Confirmed-diverges (not Not-yet-checked) because the same source explicitly documents the paper-vs-practice gap itself, not just the legal mechanism: "In practice, many long-stay remote workers use the 90-day e-visa, work online for employers and clients outside Vietnam, and leave to reset when it expires" — but "None of this is legal certainty. the rules have tightened before." Working without a required permit carries a fine of VND 15-25 million plus expulsion

unit: days (aggregate, within one calendar year or a consecutive 12-month period)
notes: New fact, 2026-07-18 (Linh). fact_label: Personal income tax — resident progressive rates

fact_label: Personal income tax — non-resident flat rate
